sources: https://www.recreation.gov/api/search?q=Bob%20Lake (and 'Bob Lake Camp'): no Bob Lake facility; the Ottawa's Scan and Pay listings are Bobcat, Henry, Moosehead and Pomeroy Lake Camps

values.note: Single site $22 a night. Fees are for the summer period when full services are provided; in early spring and late fall, with no services, fees at some areas are not charged.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/ottawa/recreation/bob-lake-campground ('Single Site: $22 per night'; 'Fees shown are for the summer recreation period when full services are provided. During the early spring and late fall when no services are provided the fees at some areas are not charged'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Campers must occupy the site the first night. After 14 days, move to another campground or dispersed site for at least 24 hours.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/ottawa/recreation/bob-lake-campground ('No reservations - first come, first serve'; 'Camping in a developed recreation site is allowed for a period not longer than 14 days, except as otherwise posted ... Campers must occupy the site the first night') + recreation.gov search (no Bob Lake listing), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Single loop of drive-in sites, screened by vegetation, that 'can accommodate tents, trailers or motor homes'; each has a picnic table, fire ring, lantern post and parking spur. No length limit posted. Eight people, two motor vehicles and at most one RV or camper trailer per site.

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/ottawa/recreation/bob-lake-campground ('a single loop with 17 campsites', 'These drive-in sites can accommodate tents, trailers or motor homes', 'No. of Sites: 17', 'Eight people and 2 motorized vehicles are allowed per campsite with a maximum of one RV or camper trailer'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Three vault toilets in the loop (one accessible); drinking water from a hand pump near the entrance. Adjacent day-use picnic area and boat landing with a concrete ramp (no launch charge).

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/ottawa/recreation/bob-lake-campground ('The camping loop contains three vault toilets, one of which is accessible. Drinking water is provided by a hand pump which is located near the campground entrance'; 'Launch Ramps: Yes, Concrete Base, no charge to launch boat'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 'The campground is scheduled to open with full services the Friday before Memorial Day. This date is subject to change.' No closing date posted.

discounts.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/ottawa/recreation/bob-lake-campground (no military discount named on the Forest Service page; the value came from the Good Sam directory), read 2026-10-25

note: Ottawa NF campground on 133-acre Bob Lake, ~18 mi SE of Ontonagon, Ontonagon RD; run by concessionaire Camp Host, LLC. Many sites near the lake; adjacent day-use picnic area, boat landing and the 1.2-mile Beaver Lodge Interpretive Trail. Shallow lake (3-17 ft) with walleye, smallmouth bass and perch. Reached via FH 16, FR 1640 (Pori Road), FR 1470 and FR 1478. --Claude
summary: FS page: 17 drive-in sites for tents/trailers/motorhomes, $22 (confirmed), first-come only (confirmed; no recreation.gov listing exists), 14-day limit, vault toilets + hand pump (potable water added), opens the Friday before Memorial Day (season added, no close date), concessionaire Camp Host, LLC. Cleared military discount (Good Sam directory only). No current alert or order for the access roads (the Oct 9-10 rally closures near Kenton have passed). Note trimmed of field restatements.
